# Using zeroh-greenfield

Inspect the repository before choosing exactly one route; return the dispatch contract below and do not execute the routed workflow.
Not this skill: delegate routed work to `greenfield-init`, `brownfield-audit`, or `stack-decision`; keep only initial trigger routing here. Use `roadmap/arc-evals/phase-29.peval.json` as the 2026-09-04 delivery evidence.

## Dispatch

| Request | Skill |
| --- | --- |
| init / new repo / scaffold | greenfield-init |
| audit / fill gaps / brownfield | brownfield-audit |
| stack choice / mobile stack | stack-decision |

Return exactly one object:

```json
{"route":"greenfield-init|brownfield-audit|stack-decision","evidence":["<repository-relative-path>"]}
```

Define `<repository-relative-path>` as an inspected marker path. If inspection cannot resolve the repository root, STOP with `route: unresolved` and the attempted path; this STOP is honor-system.

## Detection markers

Treat any existing marker as brownfield evidence. When markers disagree, use
`brownfield-audit`; it preserves existing homes and proposes only gaps.
Apply the canonical detection procedure in `../brownfield-audit/references/marker-table.md`; its root resolver refusal enforces ambiguous-root failure, while route selection remains honor-system.

| Marker | Greenfield | Brownfield |
| --- | --- | --- |
| package-manager locks | absent | one or more present |
| framework files | absent | framework config or source present |
| existing docs | absent | product, architecture, UX, or standards docs present |
| harness files | absent | AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, or another agent harness present |
| roadmap config | no marked root | canonical resolver finds a marked root or config (see `../brownfield-audit/references/marker-table.md`) |

## Ownership boundaries

- Delegate post-initialization phase planning and execution to `zeroh-roadmap`; prepare only the consumer homes and pointers it needs.
- Delegate Blade tokens, themes, and branded design work to `zeroh-design`; record only its pointers.
- Keep the trigger map in this router. Treat both ownership rules as honor-system; each routed skill names this router as the reverse boundary.

# Greenfield initialization

Use this workflow only after `using-zeroh-greenfield` finds no brownfield
markers. Load each reference only at the step that names it.
Not this skill: route initial trigger selection through `using-zeroh-greenfield`, repositories with existing markers through `brownfield-audit`, and alternative selection through `stack-decision`. Use `roadmap/arc-evals/phase-32.peval.json` as the 2026-09-04 initialized-home evidence.

## Read-only compatibility preflight

Before the interview, proposal, approval request, generator, or any consumer write,
require `roadmap` and run `roadmap config capabilities --json`. The response must be
valid JSON with `configVersion: 1`, `scopeManifestProtocol:
"scope-manifest-json-v1"`, and slots `unit-scoped`, `unit-affected`, and
`unit-impacted`. If the command is absent, exits nonzero, returns malformed or older
capabilities, print `/plugin install zeroh-roadmap@zeroh-marketplace` and STOP with
zero consumer writes.
Before approval, allow read-only repository/tool inspection and preparation in an isolated directory outside the consumer. Do not run generators or write in the consumer; specifically do not invoke `roadmap init`, including `roadmap init --help`. The CLI command-help dispatch keeps `roadmap init --help` read-only; `plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-live-evidence.test.mjs` later rejects any observed preapproval mutation.

## Interview

Load `references/prd-interview.md`. Ask one question at a time and retain
unknowns. Do not write the PRD yet.

Invoke `zeroh-greenfield:stack-decision` after the platforms and constraints
are known. It owns the stack alternatives and decision-record text.
Aim for the smallest runnable prototype that demonstrates the user's success signal.
Reuse answers already supplied; ask only unresolved questions that change the foundation.
Choose the relevant platform template (web-only, Android-only, or multi-platform),
then propose the file structure, architecture/stack rationale, test strategy,
one meaningful test and a documented local run command. Unknown product details
may remain in the PRD; unresolved tooling needed to run the prototype must be resolved.

Local prototype setup is the default. Ask about CI/release infrastructure only
when the user requests delivery or existing project requirements call for it.
Do not require sharding, a protected environment or cloud choices to start locally.
Retain unselected infrastructure as deferred; never invent credentials or authorize deployment.

## Draft proposal

Load these references in order and assemble a complete proposal:

1. `references/design-system.md` for the design-system choice or sibling handoff.
2. `references/archetypes/<name>.md` for the chosen generator and file shape, where `<name>` is `web`, `flutter`, `android`, `expo`, `nx-monorepo`, or `library-cli`.
3. `references/standards.md` for repository conventions and documentation.
4. Only for selected delivery setup: `references/ci-release-strategy.md` for its adapter, commands, lifecycle and preservation plan.
5. `references/pointers.md` for delivery/config paths and their copy/validate order.

Present every proposed operation in this exact table:

| Artifact | Target | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <artifact-or-command> | <consumer-path> | <why-it-is-needed> |

Include generator commands as artifacts. Cover the PRD,
decision records, design pointers, archetype, standards, harness files, README,
roadmap configuration, and a runnable first prototype. Include the four delivery outputs only when delivery setup was selected.
Inspect existing workflow paths first. STOP on any collision until the complete
proposal names an explicit merge decision, the preserved jobs/markers and exact
delta. Approval covers only that listed merge.

Also emit this parser-bound object with concrete values and exactly the seven gate keys:

```json
{"type":"proposal","artifacts":[{"path":"<repository-relative-path>","reason":"<reason>"}],"commands":[{"command":"<command>"}],"gates":{"lint":"<command-or-none>","types":"<command-or-none>","unit":"<command-or-none>","integration":"<command-or-none>","build":"<command-or-none>","e2e":"<command-or-none>","emit":"<command-or-none>"}}
```

When delivery is selected, include the concrete `delivery` object specified in `references/pointers.md` and bind its validation commands. Otherwise omit `delivery` and record that CI/release setup is deferred; deferred infrastructure is not an initialization failure.

Define paths relative to the consumer root, reasons as non-empty approval rationale, and `none` as an approved absence with its reason in the proposal table. `plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-live-evidence.test.mjs` rejects unsafe, broad, duplicate, or unproposed artifact paths.

## Approval gate

Obtain explicit approval of the concrete proposed changes. Reuse approval already
given for that scope; do not ask again solely to obtain a magic phrase. Native
validation fixtures use `APPROVE GREENFIELD PLAN` as their machine-observed approval
marker. STOP before consumer writes or generators without approval. A partial
approval authorizes only the selected rows; revise dependent operations accordingly. Record the
approved plan and response in `docs/PRD.md §Decisions` during execution.
The native fixture verifies its approval marker; everyday authorization is interpreted by the host, not authenticated by a hash or runner flag.

If a Blade brand requires the design sibling and it is absent, show
`/plugin install zeroh-design@zeroh-marketplace` and STOP that branch. Do not
substitute either sibling's work.

## Execute approved plan

For a multi-line executable program, load `references/prepared-program.md`: save it once, preflight it and execute its reviewed bytes. Keep simple commands direct. Execute only approved rows through the following headings in order. Run the selected archetype generator first, then write the PRD, decision records, standards, architecture and UX indexes, and harness adapters.

## Structure

Populate README structure from the selected manifest's `## File tree` and
approved `## Generator` and `## Post-steps` outputs.

## Commands

Populate README commands from the selected manifest’s `## Verify` and test conventions.
Resolve `templates/scripts/check-readme-catalog.mjs` from the installed zeroh-greenfield plugin root, copy it to consumer path `scripts/check-readme-catalog.mjs`, and run the selected manifest checker.
Record its exit code before Done.


## Delivery

Skip this section when delivery is deferred. Otherwise copy the approved planner and workflows from the installed plugin templates,
write the approved delivery configuration and fill the selected environment.
Merge approved existing workflow jobs and markers; never overwrite them silently.
Follow `references/pointers.md` to bind README commands and the CI backstop.
Installation does not authorize publishing or deployment.

## Roadmap configuration

Run `roadmap init`, then apply only the keys from `references/pointers.md`.

Never replace an existing home discovered after approval. Stop with the changed
evidence and draft a revised proposal instead.

## Verify

Follow `references/pointers.md` to execute every non-`none` gate from the consumer root, recording cwd/exit and approved absence reasons. Run the selected archetype's Verify command, the README catalog check, and
`roadmap config check`. Report each command and exit status. A failing command
keeps the initialization incomplete. Only for selected delivery setup, validate the installed workflow YAML and
execute the installed delivery planner/workflow mutation suite, recording actual
commands and terminal test totals. Record optional actionlint path/version or
unavailability; it cannot replace mandatory validation.

## Done

Return Done only when every approved artifact exists, every unapproved path is unchanged,
the approval ruling is in the PRD, the first prototype runs with its documented command, its meaningful test passes, the catalog check passes, and
`roadmap config check` exits `0`. Report the artifact paths and verification
results; do not use a prose-only success claim.

After auditing the completed tree, emit `{"type":"audit-result","proposals":[],"writes":[],"gaps":[]}` only when the skill proposes and writes nothing. `plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-live-evidence.test.mjs` later cross-checks the claim against independent observer events and tree snapshots; treat other STOP and preservation instructions as honor-system.

# zeroh-roadmap: Phase-Driven Development

Route ALL development work through the phase system — never create files/schemas/structure
ad hoc (honor-system). Invoke the CLI as `roadmap <cmd>` (fallback `node
${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/roadmap.mjs <cmd>`).

**Layout — the ONE rule about paths.** The root is DISCOVERED (`roadmap/` or `docs/roadmap/`;
`ROADMAP_ROOT` overrides; both = refused), so **write `<root>/…`, never a bare `roadmap/…`** — a
path asserted as fact is wrong in the other layout. `roadmap init [--root <dir>]` is the ONLY
sanctioned initialization path. Mechanics: `references/layout.md`.

## Routing — what the user says → what you invoke

| User says | Invoke |
|---|---|
| create / plan phase, add to roadmap | **plan-phase** |
| do / start / execute phase N | **do-phase** |
| review / verify / check phase N | **review-phase** |
| plan / create / new arc | **plan-arc** |
| do / execute / run arc | **do-arc** |
| arc sweep, pre-merge sweep | **arc-sweep** |
| release sweep, resolve release debts | **release-sweep** — manual-only; ask the user to run `/release-sweep` |
| validate arc, intent validation | **validate-arc** |
| arc landed / eval the arc | **eval-arc** (do-arc Step 9 auto-runs it) |
| show roadmap, backlog | `roadmap status` + `<root>/ROADMAP.md` |
| what's next, next phase | `roadmap status` → **do-phase** |
| code review (a diff) | the `code-reviewer` agent / the built-in review command |
| full code review, pre-release review | **full-code-review** |
| audit roadmap, roadmap health check | **audit-roadmap** |
| pause the arc | stop anywhere; files are the truth |
| resume / continue arc X | **do-arc** — `roadmap arc next` fast-forwards from disk |
| hand off / fresh session | **handoff** |
| migrate / upgrade roadmap | `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/migrate/README.md` |

NEVER handle these yourself (honor-system) — the skills carry the full protocol; your job is correct
dispatch plus the coordination below.

## Multi-session coordination (shared repos)

- The COORDINATION BOARD is `<root>/backlog.ts`'s header (lane map + release plan) — read it
  FIRST on "what next".
- `roadmap claim` BEFORE authoring a phase number (CLI-enforced: creation is the lock
  across worktrees).
- `roadmap status` shows live lanes; `roadmap arm <id>` claims an arc lane (CLI-enforced:
  refuses a taken lane — honor the refusal, never take over another session's arc).
- Cross-arc lanes ARE the sanctioned parallel path — one arc per session, gated by
  `roadmap capacity`.
- Answer lane/backlog questions from `roadmap status` + the board — never session memory.
- A consumer CLAUDE.md restating this is a mirror; on drift the CLI's behavior wins.

## Cross-cutting standards — load the reference when the work produces the artifact

Load one yourself whenever routed-to work surfaces the artifact class and the target
skill has not already:

- Writing docs, code comments, or a decision record → `references/documentation-rules.md`
- Assigning a task's `testMode` or refusing a test → `references/test-worthiness.md`
- Splitting or placing a UI component (at planning time) → `references/component-structure.md`
- Introducing any external package/font/icon/image/snippet/model → `references/external-assets-licensing.md`
- Running this protocol on a non-Claude harness (Codex) → `references/codex-tools.md`
- Scaffolding a consumer, writing a phase file's import, or a root refusal → `references/layout.md`

| Design-system files | `components.json`, `**/components.json`, `tokens/**`, `**/*theme*`, `docs/**/*design*` | Registries and token homes are evidence for design reconciliation, not permission to invent values. |

## Canonical roadmap discovery
Resolve the consumer Git toplevel first. Use `roadmapRoot(consumerRoot)` from the
installed zeroh-roadmap `cli/lib/roadmap-root.mjs`; resolve that module from the
installed plugin, never from an assumed consumer-relative plugin directory.
Pass the consumer root explicitly, retain `ROADMAP_ROOT`, and inspect
`<resolved root>/roadmap.config.json`. Do not infer absence from a top-level glob.
A marked root without a config is partial: STOP for an approved recovery proposal,
not fresh initialization. Ambiguous roots STOP with the resolver's remedy; an
explicit override retains the resolver's precedence. If the module cannot be
resolved, STOP the config branch with the sibling installation remedy rather than
implementing another candidate-order algorithm. An unmarked default destination
is not an existing configuration. Record the resolved path as gap-table evidence.

Use this read-only invocation after resolving the two absolute paths from the
installed plugin inventory and consumer Git toplevel:

```sh
node --input-type=module -e 'import { pathToFileURL } from "node:url"; import { join } from "node:path"; const { roadmapRoot } = await import(pathToFileURL(join(process.argv[1], "cli/lib/roadmap-root.mjs"))); console.log(roadmapRoot(process.argv[2]));' <roadmap-plugin-root> <consumer-root>
```

`<roadmap-plugin-root>` is the installed zeroh-roadmap plugin directory;
`<consumer-root>` is the consumer Git toplevel. A nonzero exit stops this branch.

# Stack decision

Load `references/matrices.md`. Determine which matrices apply from the approved
PRD answers, then present every row in each applicable matrix unchanged.
Not this skill: route initial trigger selection through `using-zeroh-greenfield`, leave repository changes to `greenfield-init` or `brownfield-audit`, and return only `StackDecisionOutput` here. Use `roadmap/arc-evals/phase-30.peval.json` as the 2026-09-04 delivery evidence.

## Selection

Ask exactly one selection question per applicable matrix.
Do not preselect any option before the user answers.
Present the backend matrix ONLY when the PRD answers name an API.

Accept an explicit named option or a request to revisit requirements. Do not
infer a choice from preferences. When the user chooses, ask for or summarize the
reason and confirm it before producing the ruling.
If matrix evidence is unavailable, PRD answers conflict, or the reason is unconfirmed, STOP with `status: unresolved` and name the missing evidence or conflicting answers. Treat selection and STOP behavior as honor-system.

## Callers and ownership

Accept calls from `greenfield-init` for new repositories and from `brownfield-audit` only when stack evidence is unresolved or conflicting. Keep matrices and ADR decision content in this skill and `references/matrices.md`.

Return both stack ADR decisions without implementing design or token values; delegate those values to the selected design system or `zeroh-design`.

## Output

Return one `StackDecisionOutput` containing one object per applicable matrix:

```json
{"status":"decided|unresolved","decisions":[{"adrPath":"docs/adr/0001-tech-stack.md|docs/adr/0002-design-system.md","matrix":"<matrix-heading>","options":["<exact-presented-row>"],"selected":"<named-option>","reason":"<confirmed-reason>","consequences":["<consequence>"],"revisitConditions":["<measurable-condition>"],"rulingDate":"YYYY-MM-DD"}]}
```

Define `YYYY-MM-DD` as the decision's ISO calendar date, `<matrix-heading>` as the literal heading in `references/matrices.md`, and every other placeholder as non-empty text copied or confirmed during selection. On STOP, return `{"status":"unresolved","decisions":[]}` plus the named conflict in the surrounding response.

Accumulate every applicable stack decision in the single
`docs/adr/0001-tech-stack.md`: create a labeled Options group for each presented
matrix, preserve all of its sourced rows, and add one dated ruling per group.
Never replace an earlier group's alternatives or ruling when the next matrix is
answered. Populate `docs/adr/0002-design-system.md` separately from only the
design-system options and ruling.

Add the confirmed consequences and measurable revisit conditions for every
group. Do not write either ADR until the calling workflow's approval gate has
passed.
Treat preservation of earlier groups as honor-system. Treat the no-write rule as enforced by `plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-live-evidence.test.mjs` when called inside native initialization; otherwise it is honor-system.

# Design-system step

Choose after the stack ruling and before generation. Record the choice in the
design ADR, UX canon, and roadmap pointers; never invent brand values.

## Web

Use shadcn/ui with Tailwind v4 and its CSS-first configuration. The proposal
must name the component sources and license tier before installation.

Use this `components.json` shape, replacing registry names only with approved
open registries:

```json

  "baseColor": "neutral",
  "cssVariables": true,
  "iconLibrary": "lucide",
  "registries": {
    "@magicui": "https://magicui.design/r/{name}.json"
  }
}
```

Keep one token source and generate the CSS variable projection from it. The byte-check guard fails when generated CSS bytes differ from the token source projection.

Capture `fonts | palette | spacing | ux-canon` as inputs to the UX home. Use
`external-assets-licensing.md §The tiers` to classify every external source.

# Layout — where a consumer's roadmap lives

The router (`SKILL.md`) carries the operative rule: the root is DISCOVERED, so never state a
roadmap path as a fact. This file is the mechanics, for scaffolding a consumer, writing a phase
file's import, or diagnosing a refusal.

## The root

Two candidates, in precedence order: `roadmap/` at the git toplevel (what every existing consumer
has) and `docs/roadmap/` (for a repo that keeps its workflows as sibling doc folders).

- A candidate is the root when it carries a MARKER: `roadmap.config.json` or `phases/`. An
  existing but unmarked directory is not one — a repo with a prose `docs/roadmap/` folder keeps
  reading its real `roadmap/`.
- `ROADMAP_ROOT` overrides both, absolute or relative to the repo, and is NOT probed for
  existence — an override names where the root WILL be, so `roadmap init` can scaffold into it.
- BOTH marked is a REFUSAL that names both paths and the `ROADMAP_ROOT` remedy, never a silent
  pick: two roots means two backlogs, two claim registries and two gate directories, and guessing
  one is how half a consumer's records go quietly unread.
- Neither marked resolves to `roadmap/`, so a fresh or non-consumer tree answers what it always did.

One resolver owns this — `cli/lib/roadmap-root.mjs` (`roadmapRoot`, `roadmapRootRel`,
`consumerSchemaPath`), with a shell twin at `hooks/lib/roadmap-root.sh` for the hooks. A scan
tripwire in `cli/lib/roadmap-root.test.mjs` keeps every other source out of the business of
spelling the root.

`backlog.ts`, `ROADMAP.md`, `phases/`, `arcs/`, `archive/`, `.gate/` and `arc-evals/` all sit
under the root. The schema seam resolves root-first: `<root>/lib/schema.ts`, else the legacy

missing seam is named with BOTH paths.

# Documentation rules

The one standard every doc-producing surface cites. A document that fails a rule is
edited or deleted, never explained.

## The four principles

1. **Clear and concise** — skimmable: headings, tables, bullets. No jargon, no walls
   of prose. A reader finds their answer by scanning, not reading.
2. **No duplication** — one source of truth per fact; hyperlink to it instead of
   restating it. A second copy is where staleness is born.
3. **Timeless** — concepts and patterns, never dates, version numbers, or volatile
   paths/line numbers that rot. If a fact will be false in a month, it belongs in a
   report, not a doc.
4. **Current** — an outdated doc causes more friction than a missing one. Touching a
   doc means leaving the WHOLE doc true; delete or fix stale text on sight.

## The decision bar

Docs describe the **as-built** architecture. A standalone decision record exists only
when the decision is CRITICAL — one of:

- a boundary contract (something another team or repo builds against),
- a security/privacy posture,
- expensive to reverse,

— or when the user explicitly says "document this". Every other choice lives in the
phase's `transparencyReport` and dies with the phase. An ordinary implementation
choice never mints a doc.

## Code comments are documentation too

The same bar applies in source: a comment states a non-obvious WHY in one line, or it does
not exist. Narration ("this loop now handles…"), process archaeology (phase numbers, dates,
review rounds), and restating what the code visibly does are deleted on sight — the diff
and the transparencyReport carry that story.

## Evidence is not documentation

Verification records, audit sweeps, fix logs, screenshots, parity captures: gate-report
and `transparencyReport` material. They prove work happened; they do not describe the
system. Nothing of that class lands under `docs/`.

| Bad | Good |
| --- | --- |
| `DECISION-2026-07-14-retry-backoff.md` explaining a retry constant | the constant's own comment states the non-obvious WHY; the choice is in the transparencyReport |

| A 300-line VERIFICATION.md of command outputs | the gate report carries the run; docs/ stays architecture |

# Test Strategy

**This skill is consumer-bound.** The runner, commands, layout, and mock seams are the
consumer repo's, never this plugin's. Two bindings, both in the consumer's `roadmap.config.json`:

1. **`testConventions`** — the repo's test runner, test file layout (colocated vs `__tests__/`),
   mock seam (which boundary to fake), fixture home, assertion style. Read it before writing any
   test. Absent → infer from 2-3 existing test files nearest the code under test and say so. (remedy: using-zeroh-roadmap/references/layout.md §Missing homes)
2. **`gateCommands`** — the `unit` / `integration` / `e2e` slots bind the commands (resolved by
   `roadmap gate run`).

Also check the consumer's own test-strategy document if one exists (e.g. `docs/TEST-STRATEGY.md`)
— it outranks the generic guidance below.

## Test Pyramid (generic shape — counts/runtimes are the consumer's)

| Tier | What | Bound by |
|------|------|----------|
| 1a — Unit | Pure logic, no I/O, colocated with source | the `unit` slot |
| 1b — Integration | Real wiring through the app's entrypoints, external boundaries faked | the `integration` slot |
| 2 — E2E | Real user journeys against a running instance | the `e2e` slot |

Push every assertion as far DOWN the pyramid as it can live: a rule provable in a unit test
does not belong in an E2E test.

## What gets a test at all — the declarative-artifact rule

The pyramid ranks WHERE an assertion lives; this rule decides WHETHER one exists. (testMode
assignment and the deviation protocol live in
`skills/using-zeroh-roadmap/references/test-worthiness.md` — the two homes must not drift.) Before writing
a test, name what a RED would mean. *A function's behavior changed* is a test. *A data file's
contents changed* is not: declarative artifacts (yaml/json/md, images, manifests, lockfiles, seed
data) get no bespoke test file, and never a byte-for-byte content assertion — that is a second
copy of the data that moves with it, guarding nothing. The honest guard for an artifact is its
INVARIANT (parses, references resolve, set exhaustive, ids unique), expressed as one more CASE in
a lane the consumer already runs (`gateCommands.ratchets` / `lint` / `emit`, or its documented
validator script). One scan extended with a case beats one new file per rule: a new `*.test.ts`
is permanently wired into the unit tier (inventory checks, coverage floors), while a lane leg is
one line.

This is NOT a carve-out for the loader, resolver, or schema parser that reads an artifact — that
is runtime logic and carries the full coverage targets below. Nor for checks that execute a
mapping function over a contract union, nor for the wired test a new governed surface owes.

## Coverage Targets

Coverage scores EXECUTABLE LOGIC only; a declarative artifact has no coverage number.

| Risk Tier | Target |
|-----------|--------|
| Core business rules / money math (as the consumer defines them) | 90%+ |
| Auth/security | 80%+ |
| New code | 80%+ minimum |

## Quality Bar

- Tests enforce INVARIANTS, not just outputs
- Tests fail if the bug existed — mentally revert the fix and check the test goes red
- No test capitulation (changing tests to match broken behavior)
- No no-op assertions (always-true checks) and no conditional assertions wrapped in `if` blocks
- Mock at the consumer's declared mock seam; verify call ARGUMENTS, not just call counts
- Boundary tests sit EXACTLY at thresholds

## E2E Rules & Patterns

E2E rules (real-user-flow principle, selector priority, spec structure) belong to the
consumer — look for an "E2E" section in its CLAUDE.md or test-strategy doc, and reuse its
existing spec files as the pattern source.
/** Save once, preflight before mutation, execute the reviewed bytes. Not an authorization sandbox. */
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
import { lstatSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, realpathSync, mkdtempSync, rmSync } from 'node:fs'
import { dirname, isAbsolute, relative, resolve, sep } from 'node:path'
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os'
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process'
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
const hash = bytes => createHash('sha256').update(bytes).digest('hex')
const inside = (root, path) => path === root || path.startsWith(root + sep)
const engines = {
  bash: { command: 'bash', check: ['-n'], run: ['-e', '-o', 'pipefail'] },
  python: { command: 'python3', check: ['-c', 'import ast,sys; ast.parse(sys.stdin.read())'], run: [] },
  node: { command: process.execPath, check: ['--input-type=module', '--check'], run: [] },
}
function state(cwd, path) {
  if (typeof path !== 'string' || !path || isAbsolute(path) || path.split('/').some(p => !p || p === '.' || p === '..')) throw new Error('Expected a relative file path')
  let current = cwd
  for (const part of path.split('/')) {
    current = resolve(current, part)
    try { if (lstatSync(current).isSymbolicLink()) throw new Error(`Symlink target refused: ${path}`) }
    catch (error) { if (error.code === 'ENOENT') return null; throw error }
  }
  const stat = lstatSync(current)
  if (!stat.isFile()) throw new Error(`Expected a regular file: ${path}`)
  return { sha256: hash(readFileSync(current)), mode: stat.mode & 0o777 }
}
function check(program) {
  const engine = engines[program.kind]
  if (!engine) throw new Error('kind must be bash, python or node')
  const result = spawnSync(engine.command, engine.check, { input: program.source, encoding: 'utf8', cwd: program.cwd })
  if (result.error || result.status !== 0) throw new Error(`Preflight failed: ${result.error?.message ?? result.stderr}`)
  return engine
}
export function prepare(request, directory) {
  const cwd = realpathSync(request.cwd)
  const output = realpathSync(directory)
  if (inside(cwd, output)) throw new Error('Prepared artifacts must live outside the consumer')
  if (!Array.isArray(request.paths) || !request.paths.length || new Set(request.paths).size !== request.paths.length) throw new Error('Declare unique target file paths')
  const source = readFileSync(request.script, 'utf8')
  const program = { version: 1, cwd, kind: request.kind, source, before: Object.fromEntries(request.paths.map(path => [path, state(cwd, path)])) }
  check(program)
  const bytes = JSON.stringify(program) + '\n'
  const path = resolve(output, `${hash(bytes)}.json`)
  try { writeFileSync(path, bytes, { flag: 'wx', mode: 0o400 }) }
  catch (error) { if (error.code !== 'EEXIST' || readFileSync(path, 'utf8') !== bytes) throw error }
  return path
}
export function run(path, approved = false) {
  if (!approved) throw new Error('Execution requires prior host/user approval of this artifact')
  const bytes = readFileSync(path)
  if (resolve(path) !== resolve(dirname(path), `${hash(bytes)}.json`)) throw new Error('Prepared artifact digest mismatch')
  const program = JSON.parse(bytes)
  if (program.version !== 1 || realpathSync(program.cwd) !== program.cwd || inside(program.cwd, resolve(path))) throw new Error('Invalid prepared artifact target')
  const engine = check(program)
  for (const [target, expected] of Object.entries(program.before)) {
    if (JSON.stringify(state(program.cwd, target)) !== JSON.stringify(expected)) throw new Error(`Target changed since preparation: ${target}`)
  }
  // Private execution copy of the checked bytes: children cannot consume the
  // program as stdin, and argv size limits cannot truncate large programs.
  const directory = mkdtempSync(resolve(tmpdir(), 'greenfield-program-'))
  try {
    const script = resolve(directory, program.kind === 'node' ? 'program.mjs' : 'program')
    writeFileSync(script, program.source, { flag: 'wx', mode: 0o400 })
    const result = spawnSync(engine.command, [...engine.run, script], { cwd: program.cwd, stdio: ['ignore', 'inherit', 'inherit'] })
    if (result.error) throw result.error
    return result.status ?? 1
  } finally { rmSync(directory, { recursive: true, force: true }) }
}
if (process.argv[1] && resolve(process.argv[1]) === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)) {
  try {
    const [command, path, option] = process.argv.slice(2)
    if (command === 'prepare') process.stdout.write(prepare(JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, 'utf8')), option) + '\n')
    else if (command === 'run') process.exitCode = run(path, option === '--approved')
    else throw new Error('Usage: prepared-program.mjs prepare request.json <existing-artifact-directory> | run <artifact.json> --approved')
  } catch (error) { process.stderr.write(error.message + '\n'); process.exitCode = 1 }
}
#!/usr/bin/env node
import { existsSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { basename, resolve } from 'node:path'

const args = process.argv.slice(2)
if (args.includes('--help')) {
  console.log('Usage: check-readme-catalog.mjs (--catalog <json> | --project-root <dir>) [--readme <file>]')
  process.exit(0)
}
const value = flag => { const i = args.indexOf(flag); return i >= 0 ? args[i + 1] : undefined }
const readmePath = resolve(value('--readme') ?? 'README.md')
const fail = message => { console.error(message); process.exitCode = 1 }
if (!existsSync(readmePath)) fail(`nonexistent README: ${readmePath}`)
else {
  const body = readFileSync(readmePath, 'utf8')
  const block = body.match(/<!-- repo-catalog:start -->([\s\S]*?)<!-- repo-catalog:end -->/)?.[1]
  if (!block) fail('malformed README catalog')
  else {
    const tableLines = block.split(/\r?\n/).filter(line => line.trim().startsWith('|'))
    const parsedRows = [...block.matchAll(/^\|\s*([^|]+?)\s*\|\s*([^|]+?)\s*\|\s*([^|]*?)\s*\|$/gm)]
    if (parsedRows.length !== tableLines.length || parsedRows.length < 2) fail('malformed README catalog row')
    const rows = parsedRows.slice(2).map(([, name, root]) => ({ name: name.trim(), root: root.trim() }))
    const catalogPath = value('--catalog')
    const projectRoot = value('--project-root')
    let projects
    try {
      if (catalogPath) {
        const parsed = JSON.parse(readFileSync(resolve(catalogPath), 'utf8'))
        projects = Array.isArray(parsed) ? parsed : parsed.projects
        if (!Array.isArray(projects)) throw new Error('shape')
        for (const project of projects) if (!project?.name || !project?.root || !existsSync(resolve(project.root))) throw new Error(`nonexistent catalog root: ${project?.root}`)
      } else if (projectRoot) {
        const root = resolve(projectRoot)
        if (!existsSync(root)) throw new Error('nonexistent project root')
        let name
        if (existsSync(resolve(root, 'package.json'))) name = JSON.parse(readFileSync(resolve(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8')).name
        else if (existsSync(resolve(root, 'pubspec.yaml'))) name = readFileSync(resolve(root, 'pubspec.yaml'), 'utf8').match(/^name:\s*([^\s#]+)/m)?.[1]
        else for (const file of ['settings.gradle.kts', 'settings.gradle']) if (existsSync(resolve(root, file))) name ??= readFileSync(resolve(root, file), 'utf8').match(/rootProject\.name\s*=\s*['\"]([^'\"]+)/)?.[1]
        name ??= basename(root)
        projects = [{ name, root: projectRoot }]
      } else throw new Error('choose --catalog or --project-root')
    } catch (error) { fail(`invalid catalog shape or input: ${error.message}`); projects = null }
    const duplicate = (items, label) => {
      const seen = new Set(); for (const item of items) { if (seen.has(item.name)) fail(`duplicate ${label} name: ${item.name}`); seen.add(item.name) }
    }
    duplicate(rows, 'README')
    if (projects) {
      duplicate(projects, 'catalog')
      const byName = new Map(rows.map(row => [row.name, row]))
      const catalogNames = new Set(projects.map(project => project.name))
      for (const project of projects) if (!byName.has(project.name)) fail(`missing README project: ${project.name} (${project.root})`)
      else if (byName.get(project.name).root !== project.root) fail(`README project path mismatch: ${project.name} (${byName.get(project.name).root} != ${project.root})`)
      for (const row of rows) if (!catalogNames.has(row.name)) fail(`orphan README project: ${row.name} (${row.root})`)
    }
  }
}

# scaffold-roadmap.sh — Initialize phase-driven roadmap in a project
#
# Usage: scaffold-roadmap.sh [PROJECT_DIR] [--root <dir>]
#   --root defaults to `roadmap`; `--root docs/roadmap` puts the whole consumer under
#   docs/roadmap/ beside a sibling docs folder. Everything lands UNDER the root, including the
#   schema seam — which is what lets a phase file import `../lib/schema` relatively, with no
#   tsconfig path alias. The legacy toplevel `lib/roadmap/schema.ts` seam stays recognized by
#   cli/lib/roadmap-root.mjs, so existing consumers are untouched.
#
# Creates (<root> = --root, default `roadmap`):
#   <root>/lib/schema.ts     — definePhase() + Zod shapes
#   <root>/lib/registry.ts   — Phase discovery (dynamic import + validation)
#   <root>/lib/emit.ts       — Registry emission (deterministic JSON + digest)
#   <root>/ROADMAP.md        — Validation gate + git strategy
#   <root>/backlog.ts        — Ordered execution queue
#   <root>/phases/           — Empty phases directory
#   reviews/releases/         — Release review reports directory
#   scripts/pre-review.sh     — Automated pre-review checks
#   scripts/build-dashboard.sh — Review dashboard HTML generator

set -euo pipefail

PLUGIN_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
PROJECT_DIR="."
ROOT="roadmap"
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --root)
      ROOT="${2:?--root needs a directory}"
      shift 2
      ;;
    --root=*)
      ROOT="${1#--root=}"
      shift
      ;;
    *)
      PROJECT_DIR="$1"
      shift
      ;;
  esac
done

# REFUSE rather than create a second root. Two marked roots is the ambiguity
# cli/lib/roadmap-root.mjs refuses to resolve, so scaffolding one into existence would hand the
# consumer a repo no command can read. A marker is roadmap.config.json or phases/ — the same
# two the resolver probes.
for candidate in roadmap docs/roadmap; do
  [ "$candidate" = "$ROOT" ] && continue
  if [ -f "$PROJECT_DIR/$candidate/roadmap.config.json" ] || [ -d "$PROJECT_DIR/$candidate/phases" ]; then
    echo "scaffold-roadmap: $PROJECT_DIR already carries a roadmap root at $candidate — refusing to create a second one at $ROOT." >&2
    echo "  Two roots means two backlogs and two registries, and every command would refuse to pick between them. Scaffold into $candidate, or move it first." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done

echo "=== Scaffolding zeroh-roadmap in $PROJECT_DIR (root: $ROOT) ==="

# Create directories
mkdir -p "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/lib"
mkdir -p "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/phases"
mkdir -p "$PROJECT_DIR/reviews/releases"
mkdir -p "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts"

# Copy <root>/lib templates — schema, registry, emit. This is the seam a phase file reaches with
# a RELATIVE `../lib/schema`; no tsconfig `paths` alias is required of the consumer.
for lib_file in schema.ts registry.ts emit.ts; do
  if [ ! -f "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/lib/$lib_file" ]; then
    cp "$PLUGIN_DIR/templates/$lib_file" "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/lib/$lib_file"
    echo "  Created $ROOT/lib/$lib_file"
  else
    echo "  Skipped $ROOT/lib/$lib_file (already exists)"
  fi
done

# Copy ROADMAP.md
if [ ! -f "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/ROADMAP.md" ]; then
  cp "$PLUGIN_DIR/templates/ROADMAP.md" "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/ROADMAP.md"
  echo "  Created $ROOT/ROADMAP.md"
else
  echo "  Skipped $ROOT/ROADMAP.md (already exists)"
fi

# Copy backlog.ts (ordered execution queue)
if [ ! -f "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/backlog.ts" ]; then
  cp "$PLUGIN_DIR/templates/backlog.ts" "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/backlog.ts"
  echo "  Created $ROOT/backlog.ts"
else
  echo "  Skipped $ROOT/backlog.ts (already exists)"
fi

# Scaffold roadmap/arcs/ (OPT-IN — arcs are optional; defineArc rides along via schema.ts).
# Deliberately NOT in audit REQUIRED_ARTIFACTS: a repo without arcs is fully valid.
# The directory only, never an example arc file: anything landing here is a LIVE arc, so a
# copied example makes id A with phases [1] real in a consumer that has authored none.
# templates/example.arc.ts stays installed with the plugin as reference material.

# Copy scripts

  if [ ! -f "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts/$script" ]; then
    if [ -f "$PLUGIN_DIR/scripts/$script" ]; then
      cp "$PLUGIN_DIR/scripts/$script" "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts/$script"
      echo "  Created scripts/$script"
    fi
  else
    echo "  Skipped scripts/$script (already exists)"
  fi
done

chmod +x "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts/"*.sh 2>/dev/null || true
